newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government to continue with budget voting.
newsitem.headline: Italian government to continue with budget voting.

text.p: The Italian government intends to press ahead with voting on the budget after the opposition Freedom Alliance confirmed it would continue to boycott debate on the financial package.

"They have said "no' to our every offer. It's an unprecedented breakdown," said Fabio Mussi, parliamentary party leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) -- the largest party within Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition.
He said debate on the budget, which has been suspended in the lower house of parliament since early Tuesday, would resume at 1630 GMT.
The budget is due to be approved by the lower house of parliament by November 14 after which it has to go to the Senate (upper house) for further ratification.

Silvio Berlusconi's Freedom Alliance wants the government to drop plans to introduce a reform of the fiscal system as part of the budget, saying such a review must be debated separately next year. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
